headline: Talks with Saudi Arabia are ongoing: Iran
description: Araghchi says Tehran seeks security framework without foreign military involvement
author: Reuters
article_text:
Talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia are ongoing as Tehran aims to ​reach new regional security arrangements for countries in ‌the region without foreign military involvement, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on Tuesday.

Last week, top ​officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met ​Iranian officials in Tehran, the first high-level ⁠contact between Iran and the three nations since ​August.

The US-Israeli war on Iran started in late ​February, and since then, fighting has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Riyadh said the visit was intended to open ​negotiating channels to “prevent the return of military escalation,” ​as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis had intensified ‌in ⁠recent weeks.

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated as the powerful militia advanced towards the Bab El Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the ​opposite side ​of the ⁠Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have also attacked Saudi oil ​facilities and airports, including Riyadh’s international ​airport, disrupting ⁠flights and oil exports and drawing Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in response.

Impoverished Yemen has been mired in ⁠a ​civil war since the Houthis ​pushed the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government out of the capital, Sanaa, ​in 2014.

headline: UK adventurer returns home after 28-year trek around the world
description: Karl Bushby reaches his home after crossing jungles, deserts, Arctic and English Channel
author: Reuters
article_text:
A British adventurer who has been ​walking around the world for almost three decades is due to finish his trek on ‌Monday, ending a 31,000-mile journey at the house where he grew up.

Karl Bushby has hacked through jungles in Central America, crossed the ice between Alaska and Russia, and last month swam across the English Channel on the final stretch of a voyage made ​entirely under his own steam.

Hundreds of cheering supporters greeted the 57-year-old in the square of his home ​city of Hull on Monday morning.

“After 28 years, you just couldn’t ask for more than ⁠this,” he told the crowd, before pushing on with his few possessions in a trolley, a spare tyre ​which will now never be needed slung on top.

“I guess I’ll be seeing you around,” he added. He then ​headed for his family home where his mother, his 36-year-old son and a 12-year-old granddaughter were waiting.

Bushby served in the British Army’s Parachute Regiment in his twenties.

After the breakdown of his marriage, he drew a line on a world map and set ​off, inspired by his father, who had wondered if it was possible to walk from London to New ​York.

Carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a cheap plastic camera, he started in Chile and headed north through the ‌Americas, crossing ⁠from Alaska to Russia, Mongolia and China, and back through Europe after swimming the Caspian Sea.

“Sometimes the monotony is incredible. You’re in deserts, and the landscape doesn’t change for days to weeks. That can get a little mind-bending. The same with the Arctic,” he told Reuters last year.

He originally expected to spend about 10 years on the road ​but he hadn’t anticipated ​the obstacles he’d face, amongst ⁠them a brief imprisonment in Panama, being held at gunpoint in Mexico and detention by Russian authorities for crossing the border illegally, not to mention delays from the ​2008 financial crisis and the COVID pandemic.

“This is what an odyssey in the ​21st century looks ⁠like,” he told the Telegraph newspaper.

“Half of it is literally dealing with these bureaucratic geopolitical problems, not just the environmental hurdles. There are some times where the solution is just to wait.”

Bushby told the BBC he has only spent ⁠about 15 ​of the 28 years walking, returning to Mexico periodically to sort ​out visas, logistics and corporate and media sponsorship deals.

A feature-length documentary about his journey is in production, and Bushby is planning to embark on ​a speaking tour around England in the coming weeks.

headline: UK eases permanent residency rules for care workers
description: Care workers exempt from longer waits; other migrants still face a 10-year qualifying period
author: Reuters
article_text:
Britain watered down plans on Monday to ‌impose long delays on immigrants seeking to receive permanent residence, announcing exemptions for hundreds of thousands of care workers to defuse a political outcry within the governing Labour Party.

The government had announced plans last year to require lower-skilled workers to wait 10-15 years to receive permanent residence, up ​from five years previously.

But under the plans unveiled on Monday, it said hundreds of thousands of workers in the ​care sector would now be exempt from the longer waits.

Refugees who arrived illegally by boat, ⁠however, would face additional penalties, and could now be required to wait decades.

With the exemptions, the policy would still reduce ​by 500,000 the number of migrants who arrived since 2021 and would qualify for residence by 2030, the government said.

As ​many as 1.4 million will still qualify during that period under the new rules.

The reforms are part of the government’s effort to toughen the rules, after arrivals surged following Britain’s departure from the European Union, with post-Brexit immigration policies leading to an influx of healthcare workers and students.

Initial government proposals to toughen the ​rules had sparked a backlash from unions and parts of the governing Labour Party, particularly over the fate of often low-paid workers in ​the care sector, which has struggled to fill vacancies.

“Those who contribute most will settle fastest,” interior minister Shabana Mahmood said. “Those who don’t play by the rules ‌will ⁠be refused or wait longer.”

The changes are a response to political pressure, including from Nigel Farage’s populist Reform UK party, which has surged in popularity in recent years with calls for stricter migration controls.

Concessions after backlash

Previously, legal migrants had to wait for five years before they could be granted “indefinite leave to remain”, a status which allows people to live and work in Britain permanently ​and be entitled to some ​welfare benefits.

The changes, due to ⁠take effect next year, will still double the standard qualifying period to 10 years, and be applied retrospectively to workers already in Britain.

In addition to the new exception for care workers, those ​earning at least £50,271 ($67,448) and many skilled public sector workers will be able to qualify after ​five years, while ⁠those earning more than £125,000 can qualify in just three.

The government hopes the revisions will satisfy concerns expressed by some members of the governing centre-left Labour Party.

Earlier this year, the housing secretary, Angela Rayner, described applying the rules retrospectively as “un-British”.

Last month, the energy ⁠secretary, Miatta ​Fahnbulleh, said the plans would have been tough for her family, who ​came to Britain as refugees.

The daughter of Pakistani immigrants, Mahmood has long argued that the UK needs to control immigration to protect communities like her own against ​the rise of right-wing populist policies.

headline: Strong winds nearly sweep bride away during Istanbul photoshoot
description: A gust of wind pulled a bride off balance as she posed with giant balloons near Bosphorus
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A bride in Istanbul had a frightening moment during her pre-wedding photoshoot when strong winds nearly lifted her off the ground along with a bunch of giant balloons.

The incident took place on October 26 near the Bosphorus Strait, where the bride was posing for wedding photographs.

A sudden gust caught the large balloons she was holding and pulled her towards a nearby wall, leaving her struggling to keep her balance.

The photographer quickly stepped in, grabbing the bride and helping her regain her footing.

A video of the incident has gone viral on social media, showing the force of the wind lifting the bride as she held the balloons.

She escaped without injuries and was able to continue her photoshoot afterwards.

headline: Two policemen guarding polio team shot dead in Mohmand
description: One cop injured in attack; police launch search operation to arrest attackers
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Two policemen were killed, and another injured when armed attackers opened fire on security officials assigned to protect an anti-polio vaccination team in Mohmand district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, police and officials said on Tuesday.

The attack took place in the Dog Tamanzi area of Pindiali Tehsil.

The injured officer and the bodies of the deceased were shifted to a local hospital.

The deceased were identified as Elite Force members Arabi and Zahoor.

Police cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to arrest the attackers.

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the attack and paid tribute to the two slain personnel and extended condolences to their families.

He also prayed for the injured officer’s speedy recovery, saying the personnel deployed to protect polio workers were working to secure a healthy future for the country.

Naqvi said such attacks were unacceptable and those responsible would not be spared.

headline: US midterms put Trump's grip on Congress to the test
description: Democrats need three House seats and four Senate seats to regain control of Congress, potentially limiting Trump's agenda
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Millions of Americans are voting in the US midterm elections, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate’s 100 seats up for grabs. The results will determine control of Congress and could limit or strengthen President Donald Trump’s ability to advance his agenda during the second half of his term.

The elections are widely viewed as a referendum on Trump’s presidency.

Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers, while Democrats are seeking to regain congressional control.

The House is considered the Democrats’ stronger opportunity. They need a net gain of three seats to secure a majority, with around 40 races regarded as competitive.

The Senate contest is more challenging for Democrats. Republicans hold 53 seats, while Democrats and independents have 47.

Democrats need to gain four seats to reach a 51-seat majority. Republicans can retain control with 50 seats because Vice President JD Vance can cast a tie-breaking vote in a deadlocked chamber.

A Democratic victory in the House would give the party greater power to scrutinise the Trump administration through congressional investigations, hearings and subpoenas.

It could also make it harder for the president to pass legislation and implement his policy agenda.

Trump is not on the ballot, but his presidency is central to the campaign. Republicans are relying on his support to mobilise voters, while Democrats are presenting the elections as an opportunity to challenge his administration and limit its influence.

The contest is also taking place after congressional maps were redrawn in 10 states. The Cook Political Report estimates that Republicans gained a net five seats through the redistricting process, potentially giving them an advantage.

The results could also shape the political landscape ahead of the 2028 presidential election. A strong performance by either party could provide momentum and raise the profile of potential presidential contenders.

headline: Iran-US deal still out of reach despite mediation efforts
description: Tehran insists its conditions must be met for reopening the Strait of Hormuz
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iran and the United States are far from reaching a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, despite heightened diplomatic efforts to prevent a potential return to active conflict after ​the US midterm elections.

The US carried out “defensive“ strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island overnight, with a US official saying ‌the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets.

Meanwhile, the Revolutionary Guards said they downed a US MQ-9 drone overnight in the skies over the east of the Strait of Hormuz.

“Mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington,” the senior Iranian official said, after Qatari mediators ​travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of the draft US-Iran deal that has been ​under negotiation for the past eight days.

“Tehran’s conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened,” ⁠the Iranian official cautioned, adding that nuclear talks could only start afterwards and that Tehran would not accept Washington’s “excessive demands”.

Iran’s Parliament ​Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday that the ball was in the US’ court after Tehran gave a “strong and rational response” ​to Washington.

The senior Iranian told Reuters Tehran would respond forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes.

“The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken, Iran will not submit,” Ghalibaf also said on Tuesday, adding that Tehran’s response ​to any miscalculation by the US would be unpredictable and disregard geographical constraints.

US President Donald Trump raised doubt on Monday about ​whether he would follow through on a threatened resumption of military strikes against Iran after the midterm elections on Tuesday, adding that he believed Tehran ‌wanted to ⁠make a deal as soon as possible.

headline: ECP issues show-cause notice to MQM-P over intra-party polls
description: Party given 14 days to respond to notice issued over failure to hold intra-party polls
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has issued a show-cause notice to the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to hold mandatory intra-party elections within the extended deadline of October 15, 2026.

According to the ECP, the notice was issued on October 26, giving the party 14 days to explain its failure to meet the legal requirement.

The commission said that political parties were required under the Elections Act 2017 to hold regular elections for their office-bearers and submit an election certificate within seven days of completing the process.

The ECP warned that failure to respond could lead to further legal action.

It also said that the MQM-P could lose its eligibility to obtain an election symbol, which may be withheld from the party for the next general elections if it does not conduct intra-party polls.

headline: Hina Javed's family seeks judicial commission, rejects re-investigation
description: Family questions police's impartiality, says only commission can ensure transparent probe
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The family of Hina Javed, a digital media executive who was found murdered in the bathroom of her apartment in Rawalpindi, has rejected the police decision to reopen investigations into her case and reiterated its demand for the formation of a judicial commission.

The family also expressed its lack of confidence in the Punjab Police’s impartiality.

According to the family, SSP Investigation Saifullah contacted them and asked them to visit his office to sign a request seeking the transfer of the investigation to police in another district.

However, the family said it refused to endorse the proposed re-investigation.

The family said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had advised them to seek the transfer of the investigation to another district’s police, but they remained dissatisfied with the findings of the additional inspector general (AIG).

They questioned how junior officers could reopen the case and overturn the findings of a high-level Punjab Police committee that had already cleared the nominated suspects.

The family said there is no point in another investigation by subordinate officers and maintained that only a judicial commission could ensure a transparent probe.

The family has also sent a letter to the Punjab Assembly’s parliamentary committee on interior, raising concerns over the proposed re-investigation and renewing its demand for a judicial commission.

Separately, Hina’s brother, Fahad Javed, has submitted an application to the prosecutor general under the Right to Information law, seeking copies of forensic reports and other evidence collected in the case.

The application said police had sent DNA samples, mobile phones, a laptop and other items recovered from the crime scene to the Forensic Science Laboratory in Lahore, but copies of the reports had not been provided to the complainant despite their receipt.

The family has asked authorities to provide copies of all forensic reports and other evidence in accordance with the law.

headline: IHC grants bail to TikToker Mr Patlo in stampede case
description: TikToker granted relief in case filed after two people were killed at his mehndi ceremony
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Mr Patlo until November 10 in a case registered against him in Sialkot.

According to sources, Mr Patlo appeared before the court in a wheelchair alongside his lawyer Qasim Abbasi.

The Islamabad High Court chief justice approved his protective bail after hearing his petition.

The case against Mr Patlo was registered following a stampede at his mehndi ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road in Sialkot on Saturday.

At least two people were killed and 13 others were injured.

According to the FIR registered on the complaint of police, Mr Patlo had invited people through social media, offering prizes including motorcycles and a car.

A large crowd had gathered at the venue for the event.

The FIR stated that Mr Patlo later came on stage and announced that everyone should immediately enter the ground.

As people rushed to get inside, a stampede occurred, resulting in deaths and injuries.

Police registered a case against nine nominated suspects, including Mr Patlo, while 40 to 45 unidentified people were also named in the FIR.

Rescue 1122 and other emergency teams reached the scene shortly after the incident and shifted the injured to hospital.

Videos circulated on social media showed large crowds gathered outside the stadium attempting to enter the ground.

Security guards tried to stop them, with some personnel reportedly using batons and pushing people back.

headline: From grains to chicken and milk, India faces prolonged food inflation
description: Water shortages and rising production costs are putting pressure on food supplies and prices
author: Reuters
article_text:
Indian farmer Amarsingh Gushinge wants to sow wheat and chickpeas in coming weeks to capitalise on attractive prices, but dwindling water supplies after below-average monsoon rains are preventing him from planting either crop.

Like Gushinge, millions of farmers, especially in southern and western India, are facing water shortages as they prepare to plant winter crops.

“There’s not enough moisture in the soil to sow ​the next crop, and no money left to do so either,” said Gushinge, 78, at Rajewadi village, about 400 km east of Mumbai.

The Jalna district around his village ‌has received about 48% less rain than average this year, the local weather office has said.

A weak monsoon mean farmers will have to sow winter crops under less favourable conditions, raising the risk of stunted growth and lower yields.

Lower crop yields could further stoke food inflation, with prices of sugar, pulses, wheat and rice already climbing amid a severe El Niño. Onions, ubiquitous in Indian kitchens and widely used in curries, as well as milk and poultry products, are also becoming more expensive.

A spike in ​prices of staples can anger millions of Indians - increases in onion prices have ousted state governments in elections in the past.

Higher food prices could further weaken discretionary consumption across the economy, with the weakest monsoon ​rains in more than a decade already dampening rural demand and dragging down sales of tractors and farm equipment.

Food inflation could reach around 10% in the October-December quarter, ⁠said Devendra Pant, chief economist at India Ratings and Research, citing a combination of weak rains, higher global prices and rupee depreciation.

In September, annual retail food inflation accelerated to 7.74%, pushing headline inflation to 5.54%, close to ​the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance limit of 6%.

Higher food prices will likely prompt the central bank to raise interest rates by a further 50-75 basis points, as it risks feeding into broader price pressures, Pant ​said.

He said he expects the central bank to raise rates for a second consecutive time at its December meeting, after its first hike in October.

Protein inflation

Protein has been a key driver of price increases and could prove difficult to bring down, economists said.

The central bank’s September Monetary Policy Report said animal protein and spices accounted for nearly half of the 200-basis point rise in food inflation between March and August, driven by higher feed and fodder, transport, packaging and energy costs, as well as ​bird mortality after a heat wave.

In September, meat inflation eased to 8.7% from 12.0% in August, largely due to a high base, while inflation in milk, other dairy products and eggs rose to 5.1% from 4.8%.

headline: China's 'Lipstick King' touts AI tokens in first for Singles' Day festival
description: AI tokens emerge as a new hit at China's annual shopping festival
author: Reuters
article_text:
The Singles’ Day ​shopping extravaganza in China unveiled a new attraction this year as it graduates beyond a long ‌association with cut-price cosmetics and home appliances: computing credits used to access artificial intelligence tools.

The launch is the first time AI token packages have been offered as a significant consumer product category during Singles’ Day, the world’s largest shopping festival originally held on November ​11 each year.

Top livestreamer Austin Li sold 100,000 monthly memberships of Alibaba’s QwenWork office AI service within ​half an hour during a Taobao Live broadcast on Monday, the company said.

That is equivalent ⁠to about 2 trillion AI tokens, or units of text processed by AI models.

“Chinese consumers are now very accustomed ​to using AI productivity tools,” said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at tech research firm Omdia.

Frequent users can run short ​of credits, he added, which makes extensive purchases during a sales period “a very reasonable action”.

It was unclear how much the token plans were discounted from normal prices, however.

First sale of AI products for ‘lipstick king’

The livestream was the first sale of AI products by Li, ​who earned the “Lipstick King” moniker for amassing a huge following while selling vast volumes of lipstick online.

It showcased QwenWork ​token plans, AI-enabled laptops and workplace devices. Chen Yusen, an Alibaba Group vice president and chief executive of QwenWork, also made ‌an appearance.

Li ⁠asked Chen if AI could be used to build a digital avatar of himself to chat with fans around the clock.

While AI could not replace Li, Chen responded that he hoped it could handle everyday tasks for users, freeing them to spend time with their families.

Alibaba’s Tmall has launched an AI Token Centre for the festival, offering consumer token ​packages from Alibaba Cloud, MiniMax, ​Moonshot AI and Z.AI, ⁠the e-commerce giant said.

JD.com has also introduced an AI token section bringing together services from companies including DeepSeek, Z.AI and ByteDance’s Volcano Engine.

Sales of AI token plans from October ​1 to October 20 soared 450% from the previous month, Alibaba said, while sales ​of AI personal-computer ⁠laptops surged more than 300% year-on-year in the first hour of the Nov. 11 checkout period.

Su said the tokens’ relatively long expiry periods could spur users to stock up, but warned that rapid changes in AI products may make consumers ⁠wary of ​prepaying for services at risk of being replaced or retired.

Singles’ Day, ​which has run since 2009 in an effort to spur consumer spending, earned total revenue of 1.70 trillion yuan ($255 billion) across platforms last year, ​according to third-party data provider Syntun.

The Singles’ Day ​shopping extravaganza in China unveiled a new attraction this year as it graduates beyond a long ‌association with cut-price cosmetics and home appliances: computing credits used to access artificial intelligence tools.

The launch is the first time AI token packages have been offered as a significant consumer product category during Singles’ Day, the world’s largest shopping festival originally held on November ​11 each year.

Top livestreamer Austin Li sold 100,000 monthly memberships of Alibaba’s QwenWork office AI service within ​half an hour during a Taobao Live broadcast on Monday, the company said.

That is equivalent ⁠to about 2 trillion AI tokens, or units of text processed by AI models.

“Chinese consumers are now very accustomed ​to using AI productivity tools,” said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at tech research firm Omdia.

Frequent users can run short ​of credits, he added, which makes extensive purchases during a sales period “a very reasonable action”.

It was unclear how much the token plans were discounted from normal prices, however.

First sale of AI products for ‘lipstick king’

The livestream was the first sale of AI products by Li, ​who earned the “Lipstick King” moniker for amassing a huge following while selling vast volumes of lipstick online.

It showcased QwenWork ​token plans, AI-enabled laptops and workplace devices. Chen Yusen, an Alibaba Group vice president and chief executive of QwenWork, also made ‌an appearance.

Li ⁠asked Chen if AI could be used to build a digital avatar of himself to chat with fans around the clock.

While AI could not replace Li, Chen responded that he hoped it could handle everyday tasks for users, freeing them to spend time with their families.

Alibaba’s Tmall has launched an AI Token Centre for the festival, offering consumer token ​packages from Alibaba Cloud, MiniMax, ​Moonshot AI and Z.AI, ⁠the e-commerce giant said.

JD.com has also introduced an AI token section bringing together services from companies including DeepSeek, Z.AI and ByteDance’s Volcano Engine.

Sales of AI token plans from October ​1 to October 20 soared 450% from the previous month, Alibaba said, while sales ​of AI personal-computer ⁠laptops surged more than 300% year-on-year in the first hour of the Nov. 11 checkout period.

Su said the tokens’ relatively long expiry periods could spur users to stock up, but warned that rapid changes in AI products may make consumers ⁠wary of ​prepaying for services at risk of being replaced or retired.

Singles’ Day, ​which has run since 2009 in an effort to spur consumer spending, earned total revenue of 1.70 trillion yuan ($255 billion) across platforms last year, ​according to third-party data provider Syntun.

headline: Barrister Gohar calls for dialogue to ease political tensions
description: PTI chairman urges serious and sincere negotiations to resolve outstanding issues
author: Web Desk
article_text:
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has called for dialogue to resolve political issues, warning that tensions should not be allowed to escalate further.

Speaking to the media at the Peshawar High Court on Tuesday, Gohar also criticised what he described as the government’s failure to implement a court order allowing a meeting with party founder Imran Khan at Adiala Jail.

Referring to the detention of former chief minister Sohail Afridi and the former KP Assembly speaker, Gohar welcomed the decision to refer the matter to the high court’s chief justice for the formation of a larger bench, saying court rulings should apply equally to everyone.

He said the party had sought a meeting with Imran Khan and access to medical treatment for him, but the court’s order in this regard had not been implemented.

Gohar called for an end to what he described as political victimisation and demanded the release of Imran Khan’s sisters and PTI lawmakers.

He said Imran Khan had met his lawyer, Salman Safdar, on Monday and discussed matters relating to his cases, adding that the issue could have been avoided had the meeting taken place earlier.

Criticising remarks made by PTI leader Barrister Saif, Gohar said he had not expected him to make such statements. He also questioned why PTI leaders had not been approached for comments.

Gohar reiterated that the PTI never opposed negotiations, adding that any dialogue should be held with seriousness and sincerity.

headline: Iran warns of response without 'geographical limits'
description: Military chief Maj-Gen Ali Abdollahi sets out five conditions for lasting security
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Iran’s top military commander has warned that the country’s armed forces would respond to any threat without geographical limits, while setting out five conditions Tehran considers necessary for lasting security.

Maj-General Ali Abdollahi, chief of staff of Iran’s Armed Forces and commander of the Khatam Al Anbiya Central Headquarters, said the military had the capacity to strike both the material and non-material assets of its adversaries, according to state broadcaster IRIB.

He described Iran as a “fourth centre of global power”, citing its control over the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy route, and its ability to determine the rules governing passage through the waterway.

Abdollahi said Tehran’s conditions for lasting security included an end to wars on all fronts, particularly in Lebanon and Gaza, and a rejection of negotiations conducted under military threats.

He also called for the complete removal of sanctions against Iran, the release of its frozen assets and compensation for damage caused by wars.

He said Iran considered itself a “creditor rather than a debtor” in this regard.

The remaining conditions were recognition of Iran’s sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, replacing the US-led security framework with what he called a “Hormuz mechanism”, and guarantees against renewed military attacks through security arrangements led by countries in the region.

The remarks came amid continued tensions between Tehran and Washington following the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran on February 28.

Iran has repeatedly demanded an end to the US naval blockade and the lifting of economic sanctions as part of efforts to reach a diplomatic settlement.

Separately, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who leads Tehran’s negotiating team, said on Tuesday that Iran had delivered a “firm and rational” response to Washington, adding that the United States must now decide whether to prevent another war.

Ghalibaf warned that any renewed US military action would prompt an “unpredictable” Iranian response without geographical limits.

headline: Democrats lead in key Senate races ahead of US midterms, poll finds
description: New poll shows Democrats gaining ground in Republican-held states, including Texas and Kansas
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Democratic candidates are leading in six of seven key US Senate battlegrounds, including traditionally Republican states Texas and Kansas, according to a New York Times/Siena poll released days before the midterm elections. The race in Iowa is virtually tied.

The survey found Democrats ahead in five Republican-held states — Alaska, Kansas, Maine, Ohio and Texas while the party also holds a double-digit lead in Michigan, where the Senate seat is currently held by a Democrat.

In Texas, Democratic state lawmaker James Talarico leads Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton by 50% to 43%.

In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton is ahead of Republican Senator Roger Marshall by 49% to 44%.

In Ohio, former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leads Republican Senator Jon Husted by 49% to 44%, while Democrat Troy Jackson is ahead of Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine by 51% to 45%.

In Alaska, former Democratic representative Mary Peltola leads Republican Senator Dan Sullivan by 48% to 46%.

Iowa is the closest contest, with Democrat Josh Turek leading Republican Representative Ashley Hinson by 48% to 47%.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers by 53% to 42%.

Don Levy, executive director of the Siena Research Institute, said the findings suggest Democrats could win control of the Senate, although several races remain within the poll’s margin of error.

The survey also found signs of dissatisfaction with Trump’s presidency and the Republican Party’s handling of the economy.

Only 38% of likely voters across the seven states approved of Trump’s job performance.

Democrats held a nine-point advantage over Republicans on which party voters trusted more to address the cost of living. Democratic candidates also led among independent voters in all seven states surveyed.

However, the poll offered some positive signs for Republicans. Voters who made their decisions within the previous month favoured Republican candidates by nine points, while several races remained too close to call.

The surveys were conducted from October 23 to November 1, with state-level margins of sampling error ranging from 3.4 percentage points in Texas to five points in Alaska.

Democrats need to gain at least four Republican-held seats to take control of the Senate.

headline: Early voting data points to Democratic advantage in midterm polls
description: Democrats lead in pre-election turnout, but election day voting could change picture
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Democrats have held a significant lead in early voting ahead of the US midterm elections, with pre-election turnout higher than in 2022 and a more diverse group of voters casting ballots, according to data tracked by CNN.

Data compiled by CNN, the Associated Press and analytics firm Catalist show that Democratic voters accounted for a larger share of early ballots than Republicans across 25 states.

Democrats led Republicans by 13 percentage points in early voting, an increase of more than three points compared with the same stage of the 2022 midterm elections, according to Catalist.

Early voting also increased in 28 states compared with 2022, including Texas, Michigan, South Carolina and North Carolina.

However, the data does not reveal which candidates voters supported, as ballots remain secret.

The early electorate was also more diverse than in the previous midterm elections.

Across 40 states with comparable data, White voters accounted for 71% of early voters, down from around 76% in 2022. The shares of Black and Latino voters each increased by about two percentage points.

Another notable trend was a shift towards in-person early voting, particularly among Democrats.

Mail voting appeared to account for a smaller share of ballots in several states, including North Carolina, where early in-person voting rose 36% compared with 2022, while mail voting fell 35%.

Despite the Democratic advantage in early voting, the figures do not guarantee an election outcome.

Republicans have traditionally been more likely to vote on Election Day, meaning the final balance will depend on turnout and the political preferences of those casting ballots on Tuesday.

headline: US midterm elections begin with control of Congress at stake
description: Democrats seek to wrest control of at least one chamber from Republicans
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Americans began casting ballots on Tuesday in midterm elections that will determine control of Congress and shape the remainder of President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda.

The nationwide vote will decide all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and governorships in 36 states.

State legislative positions and local offices are also up for election, alongside policy referendums in some states, according to Anadolu news agency.

The first polling stations opened at 6am local time in New York, Connecticut, New Jersey, Virginia and parts of Indiana and Kentucky, with voting getting underway at staggered times across the country.

Republicans currently hold majorities in both the House and Senate, but Democrats are aiming to capture at least one chamber, potentially limiting Trump’s ability to advance his legislative priorities.

Polls will close at different times across the country’s time zones, with the first regular closures scheduled for 6pm Eastern Time.

headline: PSX: KSE-100 settles above 168,000 level
description: Benchmark index gains 1,454.80 points or 0.87% during the trading session
author: Business Recorder
article_text:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) witnessed a strong bullish session on Tuesday amid expectations of a positive outcome from talks between the US and Iran, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index closing above the 168,000 level.

The market opened on a positive note, with buying activity pushing the index higher during the morning session. The benchmark initially gained momentum, climbing towards its intraday high of 168,469.78 points, reflecting strong investor interest.

However, the upward momentum weakened around midday as profit-taking emerged, dragging the index lower towards its intraday low of 167,308.65 points. The market subsequently moved in a relatively narrow range, with intermittent buying and selling keeping the index under pressure.

During the final trading hours, renewed buying interest helped the benchmark recover some of its earlier losses.

At close, the benchmark index settled at 168,018.86, up 1,454.80 points or 0.87%.

Analysts were of the view that the buying interest reflects a shift in how investors are reading the geopolitical situation, not an absence of risk.

“Renewed diplomatic engagement on the Middle East conflict has pulled international oil prices lower, and for Pakistan that matters directly through the import bill, the current account and inflation,” Saad Hanif, Head of Research at Ismail Iqbal Securities, told Business Recorder.

“At the same time, the market had corrected through October, so investors who stayed on the sidelines are now selectively re-entering index heavyweights in banks, E&Ps and cement, where valuations look reasonable against earnings,” he said.

However, the recovery remains headline-driven, said Saad.

“Any breakdown in peace talks or a renewed spike in oil could reverse sentiment quickly, so we would expect volatility to persist in the near term, with investors favouring fundamentally strong, dividend-paying stocks.”

Similarly, Waqas Ghani, Head of Research at JS Global, said that the equities remain positive amid “expectations of some development on talks between the US and Iran”.

On Monday, PSX closed marginally higher as support from select heavyweights was offset by renewed selling pressure in refinery stocks following a government decision to absorb higher petrol import costs through a reduction in the Petroleum Levy. The benchmark KSE-100 Index gained 154.81 points, or 0.09%, to close at 166,564.07 points.

Globally, stocks edged lower at the start of Asian trade on Tuesday, and oil prices stabilised after the previous session’s tumble, with ‌investors on edge ahead of the start of voting for the US midterm elections.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.9%, led by a decline of as much as 3.8% in Korean shares.

S&P 500 e-mini futures edged up 0.1%, while Japanese markets are closed for a holiday.

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street edged ⁠lower, with the S&P 500 slipping 0.5% as tech sector earnings weighed on investor confidence, even as data showed US manufacturing activity picked up in October amid ​strong domestic demand.

Apple shares extended losses, falling 2.8% in after-hours trading after the iPhone maker on Monday forecast lower gross margins for the crucial holiday quarter, citing rising ​memory-chip costs, and projected services revenue growth that fell well short of Wall Street expectations.

Investors are also preparing to vote in the US midterm elections, where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a challenge to keep its hold on Congress.

Opinion polls favour the Democrats to win the House, though the Senate remains too close to call. Prediction market sites Polymarket and Kalshi currently ​assign around a 75% probability that the Democrats will control the Senate.

The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) witnessed a strong bullish session on Tuesday amid expectations of a positive outcome from talks between the US and Iran, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index closing above the 168,000 level.

The market opened on a positive note, with buying activity pushing the index higher during the morning session. The benchmark initially gained momentum, climbing towards its intraday high of 168,469.78 points, reflecting strong investor interest.

However, the upward momentum weakened around midday as profit-taking emerged, dragging the index lower towards its intraday low of 167,308.65 points. The market subsequently moved in a relatively narrow range, with intermittent buying and selling keeping the index under pressure.

During the final trading hours, renewed buying interest helped the benchmark recover some of its earlier losses.

At close, the benchmark index settled at 168,018.86, up 1,454.80 points or 0.87%.

Analysts were of the view that the buying interest reflects a shift in how investors are reading the geopolitical situation, not an absence of risk.

“Renewed diplomatic engagement on the Middle East conflict has pulled international oil prices lower, and for Pakistan that matters directly through the import bill, the current account and inflation,” Saad Hanif, Head of Research at Ismail Iqbal Securities, told Business Recorder.

“At the same time, the market had corrected through October, so investors who stayed on the sidelines are now selectively re-entering index heavyweights in banks, E&Ps and cement, where valuations look reasonable against earnings,” he said.

However, the recovery remains headline-driven, said Saad.

“Any breakdown in peace talks or a renewed spike in oil could reverse sentiment quickly, so we would expect volatility to persist in the near term, with investors favouring fundamentally strong, dividend-paying stocks.”

Similarly, Waqas Ghani, Head of Research at JS Global, said that the equities remain positive amid “expectations of some development on talks between the US and Iran”.

On Monday, PSX closed marginally higher as support from select heavyweights was offset by renewed selling pressure in refinery stocks following a government decision to absorb higher petrol import costs through a reduction in the Petroleum Levy. The benchmark KSE-100 Index gained 154.81 points, or 0.09%, to close at 166,564.07 points.

Globally, stocks edged lower at the start of Asian trade on Tuesday, and oil prices stabilised after the previous session’s tumble, with ‌investors on edge ahead of the start of voting for the US midterm elections.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.9%, led by a decline of as much as 3.8% in Korean shares.

S&P 500 e-mini futures edged up 0.1%, while Japanese markets are closed for a holiday.

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street edged ⁠lower, with the S&P 500 slipping 0.5% as tech sector earnings weighed on investor confidence, even as data showed US manufacturing activity picked up in October amid ​strong domestic demand.

Apple shares extended losses, falling 2.8% in after-hours trading after the iPhone maker on Monday forecast lower gross margins for the crucial holiday quarter, citing rising ​memory-chip costs, and projected services revenue growth that fell well short of Wall Street expectations.

Investors are also preparing to vote in the US midterm elections, where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a challenge to keep its hold on Congress.

Opinion polls favour the Democrats to win the House, though the Senate remains too close to call. Prediction market sites Polymarket and Kalshi currently ​assign around a 75% probability that the Democrats will control the Senate.

headline: Investors ready for possible shake-up in Congress as Election Day arrives
description: Investors brace for potential volatility as Democrats seek control of Congress
author: Reuters
article_text:
Investors are weighing the market implications of a possible shift in control of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, focused on whether a strong Democratic showing could pave the way for greater volatility in ​asset prices, particularly the AI trade, which has been a main driver for markets.

The midterms come at ‌a fragile time for markets, with a swoon in AI shares causing investor unease that could be exacerbated by the election results. Tuesday’s outcome could hold broad implications for market-sensitive areas including the AI data-centre buildout, the US fiscal outlook, defence spending, and regulation in areas such as healthcare, banking and cryptocurrencies.

President ​Donald Trump’s Republican Party has controlled both chambers of Congress during the first two years of his second term. Opinion polls show the Democrats are likely to take the House, while the Senate is too close to call.

“While probabilities increasingly favour a Blue sweep, several tightly contested Senate races leave open some possibility of Republican control of ​the Senate or, conversely, a greater than expected Democratic foothold in the Senate,” Scott Chronert, US equity strategist at Citigroup, ​said in a research note. “Equity market reaction is likely positive in the former case and negative in the latter.”

Strategists at UBS Global Wealth Management have assigned a 50% probability of a Democratic sweep, a 40% chance of Democrats winning the House while Republicans retain the Senate, and ​a 10% probability that Republicans hang onto both chambers.

“The most visible effects of a change in congressional control would likely ​be greater oversight of the administration and more difficult fiscal negotiations,” Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, said ‌in a ⁠note on Monday.

A Democratic-led Congress could exert greater scrutiny over AI companies, in part due to growing public opposition to data centers, a risk for a market that has been lifted by such investment spending. While analysts doubt any viable legislation would severely undermine the data-centre buildout regardless of the election outcome, they expect a Democratic sweep to lead to investigations ​into the technology sector.

Many investors have ​said they are eager ⁠to get past the elections, which have hung over the markets for the last several weeks. Since 1970, in midterm election years, the S&P 500 index has gained in every six-month ​period following the election, according to Edward Jones.

While equity volatility has increased in recent ​sessions, option-market traders ⁠are nonetheless not bracing for a massive stock market move following the election results.

Options on the S&P 500 index are priced for a move of about 0.8% in either direction on Wednesday, slightly higher than the 0.6% average implied daily move over the ⁠past month, ​according to ORATS data.

“We could see some volatility come out once there ​is a clear result, but I wouldn’t assume all that uncertainty disappears Wednesday morning,” said Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments. “Election hedges can ​expire; geopolitical risk doesn’t have an expiration date.”

headline: Trump's Justice Dept identifies where US election monitors will be in the 50 states
description: Justice Department calls it the largest Election Day monitoring effort in US history
author: Reuters
article_text:
The US Justice Department said on Tuesday it was deploying 1,000 election monitors and observers ​to all 50 states in what it called ‌the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history.

A Justice Department statement identified which jurisdictions within the states would receive monitors and observers.

Department ​officials have said priorities include areas with a history ​of voter access issues and places with competitive ⁠races that could be targets of voter intimidation.

The ​Trump administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, ​pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics view ​the moves as federal overreach.

The expanded federal monitoring program ​led several states to issue new guidelines to local election officials ‌and ⁠poll workers about the limited authority DOJ observers will have on Election Day.

“Election monitors will be checking for compliance with the federal voting rights statutes that fall ​within the jurisdiction ​of the (Civil ⁠Rights Division),” the Justice Department statement said.

Some state and local laws allow election officials to ​prevent DOJ monitors from being present inside ​polling ⁠locations. DOJ staff cannot conduct investigations on the spot or otherwise stop anyone from voting.

The number of monitors is ⁠roughly ​triple the number in the last ​midterm election. The deployment would be the largest observation effort in ​the department’s history.

headline: Security forces kills 17 militants in two operations in Balochistan: ISPR
description: Pakistan Army soldier martyred during exchange of fire
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Security forces killed 17 militants in two separate intelligence-based operations in Pakistan’s southwestern Balochistan province, while a Pakistan Army soldier was also martyred during an exchange of fire, ISPR said on Tuesday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the operations were conducted on November 1 in Kachhi and Kharan districts following intelligence reports about the presence of militants affiliated with what it described as Indian-backed proxy groups.

In the first operation, security forces targeted militants in the Sanni area of Kachhi district after they attempted to establish a blockade. The attempt was thwarted, and 10 militants were killed, with weapons and ammunition recovered from their possession, the ISPR said.

In a separate operation in Kharan district, security forces identified and destroyed a militant hideout. Seven militants were killed during an intense exchange of fire, while weapons and ammunition were also recovered, according to the statement.

A Pakistan Army soldier, Sepoy Hikmatullah, was killed during the operation in Kharan. He was 25 years old and belonged to Karak district, the military said.

The ISPR said clearance operations were underway in both areas to eliminate any remaining militants.

It added that counterterrorism operations would continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam framework, approved by the Federal Apex Committee under the National Action Plan, until terrorism and its alleged foreign support were eliminated.

headline: Petroleum minister promises relief to LPG consumers through market reforms
description: Government abolishes quota-based distribution and establishes funds to support vulnerable households
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan is introducing a series of reforms to open the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector to competition, curb monopolistic practices and bring down prices, Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Tuesday.

Addressing a press conference alongside Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar, Malik said the government had decided to abolish the existing quota-based distribution mechanism and introduce transparent auctions to encourage competition and ensure affordable fuel for consumers.

Tarar said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the introduction of a merit-based and transparent system in the LPG sector by ending monopolistic practices and abolishing the long-standing discretionary quota system.

He termed the initiative a historic step, saying no previous government had attempted to dismantle the monopoly of a few individuals and introduce a competitive mechanism based on merit.

Malik said the government aimed to ensure the availability of natural gas through pipeline networks wherever possible, while providing LPG at affordable prices to households not connected to the gas network.

Explaining the international pricing mechanism, Malik said Saudi Aramco’s monthly Contract Price (CP), based on propane and butane, served as an international benchmark for LPG, similar to Platts for petroleum products.

He said the Saudi Aramco CP had increased from $540 per tonne in March to $756 per tonne, prompting the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) to revise domestic prices accordingly.

Pakistan currently meets around 70 per cent of its LPG requirements through imports, while domestic production stands at approximately 2,200 to 2,500 tonnes per day, he said.

Malik said the existing free-on-board (FOB) pricing mechanism did not adequately account for import-related costs, encouraging the growth of informal and grey-market channels.

The government had therefore decided to introduce competition and encourage public and private companies to import LPG from international markets at competitive prices, he added.

Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Sui Southern Gas Company and Pakistan LNG Limited, along with other state-owned entities, had been directed to arrange bulk LPG supplies through government-to-government and business-to-business arrangements, the minister said.

These companies would publicly disclose monthly cost components, including Saudi Aramco’s CP, premiums, freight charges and other expenses, on their websites to ensure transparency.

Private-sector companies would also be encouraged to import LPG, while increased competition and supply were expected to help bring prices down, he said.

Referring to prevailing international market conditions, Malik said LPG was trading at a premium of $300 to $400 per tonne over the Saudi Aramco CP.

Taking all costs into account, the prevailing spot-market price was estimated at Rs450 to Rs500 per kilogram, he said, adding that the government would publicly disclose relevant pricing details and welcome any importer capable of bringing the product at a lower price.

Announcing the end of the existing quota-based distribution mechanism, Malik said domestic LPG production would instead be auctioned in transparent lots of five to 10 tonnes among OGRA-licensed companies.

Auction results would be made public, with the process monitored by the Petroleum Secretary and OGRA chairman, he added.

To protect consumers in remote and hard areas, the government would ensure proper utilisation of the 10 per cent LPG quota allocated under the policy, Malik said.

State-owned companies would procure this quota directly from producers and distribute it fairly among designated districts in consultation with provincial chief secretaries.

Additional revenue generated through the auction mechanism would be channelled into a price stabilisation fund and a vulnerable consumers’ protection fund, he said.

The funds would help provide LPG at subsidised rates to deserving consumers identified under criteria to be developed in consultation with the Benazir Income Support Programme and provincial governments.

Malik said the Competition Commission had also been asked to take measures against cartelisation and anti-competitive practices, while OGRA would strengthen its licensing and audit mechanisms to prevent hoarding and profiteering.

The National Explosives Department would oversee safety standards, including the quality and testing of LPG cylinders and transportation bowsers, he added.

Tarar said the government was also taking measures to protect consumers from the impact of the global energy crisis, adding that the prime minister had initially provided subsidies worth Rs133 billion to prevent increases in petrol and diesel prices and ensure fuel availability.

Subsequently, a targeted subsidy mechanism was introduced through the Fuel Relief Scheme to extend assistance to deserving and underprivileged segments of society, he said.

He added that OGRA had started publishing all relevant details on its website as part of the government’s efforts to improve transparency and strengthen regulatory oversight.

The new LPG arrangements were expected to become fully operational before winter, Malik said.

He added that the current crisis should also serve as an opportunity to strengthen Pakistan’s energy infrastructure, develop storage and import facilities and make the country more resilient to future supply disruptions.

The ultimate objective was to establish a transparent and competitive LPG market that ensured affordable fuel, improved consumer services and protection for the most vulnerable sections of society, Malik said.

Pakistan is introducing a series of reforms to open the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector to competition, curb monopolistic practices and bring down prices, Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Tuesday.

Addressing a press conference alongside Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar, Malik said the government had decided to abolish the existing quota-based distribution mechanism and introduce transparent auctions to encourage competition and ensure affordable fuel for consumers.

Tarar said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the introduction of a merit-based and transparent system in the LPG sector by ending monopolistic practices and abolishing the long-standing discretionary quota system.

He termed the initiative a historic step, saying no previous government had attempted to dismantle the monopoly of a few individuals and introduce a competitive mechanism based on merit.

Malik said the government aimed to ensure the availability of natural gas through pipeline networks wherever possible, while providing LPG at affordable prices to households not connected to the gas network.

Explaining the international pricing mechanism, Malik said Saudi Aramco’s monthly Contract Price (CP), based on propane and butane, served as an international benchmark for LPG, similar to Platts for petroleum products.

He said the Saudi Aramco CP had increased from $540 per tonne in March to $756 per tonne, prompting the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) to revise domestic prices accordingly.

Pakistan currently meets around 70 per cent of its LPG requirements through imports, while domestic production stands at approximately 2,200 to 2,500 tonnes per day, he said.

Malik said the existing free-on-board (FOB) pricing mechanism did not adequately account for import-related costs, encouraging the growth of informal and grey-market channels.

The government had therefore decided to introduce competition and encourage public and private companies to import LPG from international markets at competitive prices, he added.

Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Sui Southern Gas Company and Pakistan LNG Limited, along with other state-owned entities, had been directed to arrange bulk LPG supplies through government-to-government and business-to-business arrangements, the minister said.

These companies would publicly disclose monthly cost components, including Saudi Aramco’s CP, premiums, freight charges and other expenses, on their websites to ensure transparency.

Private-sector companies would also be encouraged to import LPG, while increased competition and supply were expected to help bring prices down, he said.

Referring to prevailing international market conditions, Malik said LPG was trading at a premium of $300 to $400 per tonne over the Saudi Aramco CP.

Taking all costs into account, the prevailing spot-market price was estimated at Rs450 to Rs500 per kilogram, he said, adding that the government would publicly disclose relevant pricing details and welcome any importer capable of bringing the product at a lower price.

Announcing the end of the existing quota-based distribution mechanism, Malik said domestic LPG production would instead be auctioned in transparent lots of five to 10 tonnes among OGRA-licensed companies.

Auction results would be made public, with the process monitored by the Petroleum Secretary and OGRA chairman, he added.

To protect consumers in remote and hard areas, the government would ensure proper utilisation of the 10 per cent LPG quota allocated under the policy, Malik said.

State-owned companies would procure this quota directly from producers and distribute it fairly among designated districts in consultation with provincial chief secretaries.

Additional revenue generated through the auction mechanism would be channelled into a price stabilisation fund and a vulnerable consumers’ protection fund, he said.

The funds would help provide LPG at subsidised rates to deserving consumers identified under criteria to be developed in consultation with the Benazir Income Support Programme and provincial governments.

Malik said the Competition Commission had also been asked to take measures against cartelisation and anti-competitive practices, while OGRA would strengthen its licensing and audit mechanisms to prevent hoarding and profiteering.

The National Explosives Department would oversee safety standards, including the quality and testing of LPG cylinders and transportation bowsers, he added.

Tarar said the government was also taking measures to protect consumers from the impact of the global energy crisis, adding that the prime minister had initially provided subsidies worth Rs133 billion to prevent increases in petrol and diesel prices and ensure fuel availability.

Subsequently, a targeted subsidy mechanism was introduced through the Fuel Relief Scheme to extend assistance to deserving and underprivileged segments of society, he said.

He added that OGRA had started publishing all relevant details on its website as part of the government’s efforts to improve transparency and strengthen regulatory oversight.

The new LPG arrangements were expected to become fully operational before winter, Malik said.

He added that the current crisis should also serve as an opportunity to strengthen Pakistan’s energy infrastructure, develop storage and import facilities and make the country more resilient to future supply disruptions.

The ultimate objective was to establish a transparent and competitive LPG market that ensured affordable fuel, improved consumer services and protection for the most vulnerable sections of society, Malik said.
